note: Configuration and hand-read research for Tools/instant/build.py (WP02: instant.json). Everything numeric the build stores is fetched by build.py from the URLs below or read from the repository's own data files; this file holds what cannot be fetched: which rows and columns to read, the crosswalks to the scene's tiers (drawing choices, marked assumed), labels for the NIPA lines whose register names are only a parent's name, and slots for values a person reads by hand (left null, with the reason, where the source refused automated requests on 2026-11-03).

classes.basis: household income rank, in the Federal Reserve DFA's six income groups (MODALITIES.md rule 9 and section 2.7)

dfa.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Distributional Financial Accounts (DFA), household balance sheets by income percentile group, detailed levels (dfa-income-levels-detail.csv)
dfa.sourceWealth: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Distributional Financial Accounts (DFA), household balance sheets by wealth percentile group, detailed levels (dfa-networth-levels-detail.csv)
dfa.sourceOrder: classes by income from the mirror pinned to circuit.json's release; if the mirror cannot be read, the same file from the Fed's current download (a later release, said so); if no income-group file can be read at all, classBasis 'wealth' with the four wealth groups from the mirror, else the Fed's download, else circuit.json groups (net worth and households only). --simulate-missing takes dfa-income (the income file everywhere), dfa-wealth (the wealth file everywhere), dfa-mirror (both mirror files) and dfa-zip (the Fed's download), comma-separated

debtComparisonZ1.what: Fed Z.1 debt of households and nonprofit organizations (debt securities and loans), the nearest measure to the spec's $20.6T in the repository
debtComparisonZ1.note: history.json's 2025 point is Z.1 debt at 2025:Q3 over 2025 disposable income (both pre-update vintage), so this product recovers that debt level only approximately. It is a wider measure than the DFA's mortgages + consumer credit: it includes nonprofit organizations and every loan and debt security.

mirror.why: MODALITIES.md section 12 asks for the same release as circuit.json, which read the bdecon/US-chartbook GitHub mirror of the Fed's files (circuit.json sources and groupNotes.source); the Fed's own download now serves a later release, so the mirror is pinned to the last commit that changed the files, which holds the release with data through 2026:Q1
mirror.release: June 2026 release (data through 2026:Q1), the release circuit.json used

official.note: the Fed's current download (read for the newer release's latest quarter and for the DFA's own definitions)

instruments.name: corporate equities and mutual fund shares (outside DC pensions)
columns: Corporate equities and mutual fund shares

instruments.name: private businesses (equity in unincorporated business, incl. real estate rented out)
pension entitlements (defined benefit, defined contribution and annuities)
debt securities (US government and municipal; corporate and foreign bonds)
consumer durables (cars, furniture, appliances, at current cost)
other assets (loans held, life insurance reserves, miscellaneous)
consumer credit (cards, student and vehicle loans)
other liabilities (bank loans n.e.c., other loans and advances, unpaid life insurance premiums)
columns: Deferred and unpaid life insurance premiums

dpi.source: BEA, Distribution of Personal Income, national summary file (all years 2000-2024; 2024 provisional)
dpi.rankingWhy: households ranked by income before taxes (size-adjusted), the closest of BEA's two rankings to the DFA's ranking by household income before taxes

components.concept: Rental income of households with capital consumption adjustment
Household current transfer receipts from business (net)
Contributions for government social insurance, domestic

dpi.leftOut: Household current transfer receipts from nonprofit institutions (NIPA Table 2.9 line 32) are a transfer inside 'persons' in Table 2.1, so they have no Table 2.1 total to scale to and are left out.

joint.source: BEA and BLS, joint distribution of disposable personal income, personal consumption expenditures and personal saving, summary file (2000-2023)
joint.rankingNote: BEA publishes consumption and saving by group only with households ranked by size-adjusted disposable income

bea.sourceYearWhy: 2023 is the latest year for which BEA publishes every piece used: income components by decile, a point estimate of the top 1%'s share (2024 is provisional and gives the top 1% as an interval) and the distribution of consumption and saving (2000-2023)

circuitVintage.why: MODALITIES.md and WP10's acceptance quote circuit.json's 2025 accounts, from before BEA's annual update of 30 September 2026 (PCE $20.95T; class gross income $28.12T = personal income + contributions); the same group shares on those totals let M1 use one vintage throughout if the spec keeps it, while the main block follows the current flat files

cbo.why: www.cbo.gov answered every automated request on 2026-11-03 with HTTP 403 and a DataDome CAPTCHA page ('Please enable JS and disable any ad blocker'); the build does not get around bot checks
cbo.wanted: CBO, The Distribution of Household Income (latest year): for the top 1% and for the top quintile, labor income, business income, capital income excluding capital gains, social insurance benefits plus means-tested transfers, and federal taxes, so each top-1% share of the top fifth can be read by hand

fallback.summary: the top 1%'s total income and disposable income are BEA's published top-1% shares; its owners' income is the top fifth's, split between 80-99% and the top 1% in proportion to the matching DFA holdings of the same income groups; its benefits and business transfers are the top fifth's per household; its taxes are BEA's top-1% personal income (households ranked by personal income) less its top-1% disposable income (households ranked by disposable income, the only ranking under which BEA publishes it), a mix of two rankings that likely understates the income-ranked top 1%'s taxes (the size per 0.1 pt of disposable-income share is in steps.rankingMix and taxesSensitivity); its pay is what is left of its personal income, with social-insurance contributions at the top fifth's ratio to pay

dividends: Corporate equities and mutual fund shares

keyNotes.proprietors: proprietors' income follows equity in unincorporated business
keyNotes.rental: rental income of households (mostly the imputed rent of owner-occupied homes, net of mortgage interest) follows home equity
keyNotes.dividends: personal dividend income is paid on directly held shares and funds (DC-pension holdings excluded, as in the DFA column)
keyNotes.interest: personal interest income includes imputed interest on pension and life-insurance reserves, so the key holds deposits, bonds, loans held and those reserves

ce.source: BLS Consumer Expenditure Surveys, quintiles of income before taxes (Table 1101 series), annual means per consumer unit
ce.why: www.bls.gov serves its tables only to browsers ('Access Denied' to automated requests on 2026-11-03); its Public Data API is the sanctioned automated route
ce.patternNote: LB01 = quintiles of income before taxes; group 01 = all consumer units, 02 = lowest 20% ... 06 = highest 20%; M = mean
ce.sixGroupsYearWhy: the spec's year and spending.json's: MODALITIES.md section 12 and MODALITIES-PLAN.md WP02 item (3) name BLS CE 2024, and spending.json byQuintile (which M1 also reads) is CE 2024; CE 2025 is stored in byQuintile beside it, for when the spec owner moves both to 2025
ce.notPurchasesNote: cash contributions and personal insurance and pensions (mostly Social Security and pension contributions) are transfers and contributions, not purchases of goods and services
ce.top1Assumption: assumed: the 80-99% group and the top 1% spend in the top fifth's proportions (the CE ranks consumer units in fifths and barely samples the top 1%)

nipa.source: BEA, National Income and Product Accounts, annual flat files (NipaDataA.txt with SeriesRegister.txt and TablesRegister.txt)

stubs.22: Government consumption expenditures and gross investment

stubs.26: Other current transfer payments to the rest of the world

stubs.34: To residents other than general government
stubs.49: Federal net lending or net borrowing (-)

stubs.15: Federal: compensation of general government employees
stubs.50: State and local: compensation of general government employees

T61600D.note: Lines 8-33 are profits with inventory valuation adjustment only: BEA allocates the capital consumption adjustment to industries only in total (lines 1-7).

profitsCrosswalk.label: assumed: mapping
profitsCrosswalk.basis: corporate profits with inventory valuation adjustment, domestic industries (NIPA Table 6.16D line 9)

tiers.names: manufacturing (15) less computer and electronic products (19) and petroleum and coal products (25); wholesale trade (28); retail trade (29); transportation and warehousing (30)
financial incl. Federal Reserve banks (10); other nonfinancial (32)

impurities: Other nonfinancial (line 32) also holds agriculture and mining (raw in the scene), construction (manufacturing & infrastructure) and computer systems design (tech: the scene's software industry includes NAICS 5415); BEA does not split it.
Other durable goods (inside manufacturing, line 22) holds primary metals, which the scene counts as raw.
The rest of the world (line 33) is not a US industry and is left out of the tiers.
profitsCrosswalk.tech: Tech = computer and electronic products + information (MODALITIES-PLAN.md WP02), the scene's hardware (NAICS 334) and its software, internet and media & telecom industries (NAICS 51)

sectorWeights.why: www.spglobal.com answered every automated request on 2026-11-03 with HTTP 403 'Security Controls Triggered'; the build does not get around bot checks, so the weights wait for a person to read the factsheet
sectorWeights.wanted: GICS sector weights of the S&P Total Market Index (or the S&P 500, said so), read by hand from the S&P Dow Jones Indices factsheet: index, as-of date, page and the quoted line for each sector

gicsCrosswalk.label: assumed: mapping
notes: Materials holds chemicals and packaging (manufacturing in the scene) beside metals and mining.
Health Care holds drug makers (manufacturing in the scene, as circuit.json files Eli Lilly and Johnson & Johnson) beside hospitals and insurers (services).
Consumer Discretionary holds hotels, restaurants and education services (services in the scene) beside carmakers and retailers.
Communication Services holds Alphabet, Meta, Netflix and the telecom carriers: the scene's internet and media & telecom industries.

publicDebt.definition: federal debt held by the public (marketable and nonmarketable Treasury securities held outside federal government accounts); state and local debt is separate

debtToThePenny.source: US Treasury, Fiscal Data, Debt to the Penny (debt_to_penny endpoint)

h41.source: Federal Reserve statistical release H.4.1, Factors Affecting Reserve Balances, 3 September 2026, Table 1
h41.note: the Wednesday level nearest the end of August (Wednesday 2 September 2026); securities held outright at face value, incl. inflation compensation on inflation-indexed notes and bonds

tic.source: US Treasury, Treasury International Capital (TIC) system, Table 5: Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities

hyperscalers.definition: capital expenditures as each firm's cash purchases of property and equipment in its cash-flow statement, finance leases out, calendar 2025 (Oracle, whose fiscal year ends in May: its four quarters from December 2024 to November 2025)
hyperscalers.why: it is the only definition the stored filings give for all five firms: Microsoft's and Meta's headline figures add finance leases, Alphabet's, Amazon's and Oracle's do not, and the stored data have no finance-lease additions for Alphabet or Oracle in calendar 2025
